title: Diabetic foot screen: press a 10 g monofilament perpendicular until it bends at four sole sites, testing beside a callus
instruction: Screen the training manikin's foot with the monofilament: press it perpendicular to the sole until it bends, about 1.5 s, at the big toe and 1st, 3rd and 5th metatarsal heads, beside any callus; then put the pen back.
context: Medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00, about 811,000 US jobs, BLS 2024) and registered nurses do the annual diabetic foot exam in primary care. Its sensation test (IWGDF 2019, ADA) touches a 10 g nylon monofilament to the plantar hallux and the 1st, 3rd and 5th metatarsal heads: perpendicular to the skin, pressed until it bends, about 2 s from approach to removal, never slid, and never on callus, ulcer or scar (test at its edge). An angled, jabbed, slid or on-callus touch gives a false result, and missed loss of sensation means unnoticed foot ulcers and amputations. The sole is curved, so every site needs its own approach line and a stop inside the filament's 11 mm bend window.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench), arm bases at y +-30.5. Foot: a rigid life-size adult right foot model (skin sRGB 224, 172, 145; 26.5 cm heel to toe, 10.5 cm across the forefoot) on a dark (45, 47, 50) sloped stand, 3 kg, loose on the bench: the sole faces the robots, tipped back 30 deg from vertical and turned 30 deg toward the robots' left; the seed shifts the stand -1.2 to +1.2 cm along y. Test sites (skin point; outward normal as x, y, z) with the stand unshifted: plantar hallux (48.2, -6.9, 25.3; -0.63, 0.18, 0.76), 1st metatarsal head (45.8, -6.2, 20.7; -0.88, 0.08, 0.46), 3rd (47.0, -3.0, 21.0; -0.75, 0.43, 0.50), 5th (48.8, 0.1, 19.3; -0.47, 0.76, 0.45); each site lies on its own flat skin pad (2.7 to 4.2 cm across) facing along its normal. One seeded site carries a yellow (226, 196, 84) callus, a disc 18 mm across and 1.5 mm proud, centred on the site. Pen: Owen Mumford Neuropen class, blue (30, 90, 190) barrel 16 mm across and 14.0 cm long, 15 g, white nose 6 mm long; a white 10 g (5.07) nylon monofilament 38 mm long comes out of the nose along the axis (it buckles at about 0.1 N, 10 g); it has a slight set, curving toward a white stripe printed along the barrel, its tip 2.9 mm off the barrel's axis. It lies loose across two grey (120, 124, 128) cradle posts 11.6 cm apart (slots 19 mm wide, barrel axis 4.5 cm up) at x 28, centred on y -16 (the seed shifts the pen -0.6 to +0.6 cm along the cradle), filament end toward +y, stripe facing the robots.
scoring: Score 0 if at any point the filament touches the callus, the pen's barrel touches the foot, the pen falls off the bench, or the foot model moves more than 20 mm. Otherwise 0.25 for each site whose first contact was a correct test: the filament tip landed within 8 mm of the site (on the callus site: 2 to 8 mm outside the callus edge), the barrel tip came within 35 mm of the skin (the filament bent) but never closer than 24 mm, the pen's axis stayed within 15 deg of the skin normal and the tip within 3 mm of its landing point while bent, and the contact lasted 1.0 to 3.0 s. A site's later contacts never count. Four sites score 0.75 until the pen lies back in its cradle with no gripper centre within 5 cm of it: then 1.0 (success, held 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lay the pen back across its cradle posts, filament toward the robots' left, its centre within 6 mm of the cradle's centre (the seed sets the offset). Put the foot stand back with the 3rd metatarsal head at x 47.0, its y between -4.2 and -1.8 (seeded), and move the callus to the seeded site. Real trial: re-ink the site rings and replace the monofilament after 70 to 90 uses (IWGDF).
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. Rigid foot model of boxes and capsules with a flat skin pad at each site; sizes from adult anatomy (estimates). Filament: 4 rigid capsule links on sprung hinges (1.0e-3 N m/rad, linear buckling load 0.098 N) that bend in one plane; drawn and collided 1.6 mm thick (real 0.4 mm), link mass 0.1 g centred on each hinge for solver stability. The callus is painted (no collider). Touches, angles and slide are scored from geometry. Masses are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, seed 0); scripted demo: 1.0 (seeds 0-7, success at steps 1104-1157); do nothing, random joints, random reaches, naive straight-ahead press: 0.0; press along the sole's mean normal: 0.25 (only the 3rd metatarsal head, where that normal is right)
